Nvidia has already blamed rising prices on industry-wide memory supply constraints, and those pressures may not ease soon.

For investors, the issue is not simply that DGX Spark is getting more expensive.
The broader question is whether higher memory costs begin to pressure Nvidias pricing strategy, customer budgets or hardware configurations across its AI lineup.
So far, strong demand appears to be giving Nvidia room to pass much of the pressure through to customers.
But if memory prices remain elevated, customers may become more selective about how aggressively they expand AI infrastructure.
That makes memory supply one of the more important cost variables to watch as Nvidia tries to preserve both demand and margins through the next phase of the AI buildout.
